clue.text: Shady lady found at respectable kind of address?

definitions.meaning: a woman who runs a brothel is called by this title
the polite way to speak to a woman whose name you do not know

explanation.surface: A woman of dubious character turns up at a smart residential address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a street location, but it means a form of words used to speak to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the courteous title for a lady and slang for a brothel keeper.

clue.text: Not said to attend us congregation

indicators.note: a congregation is a gathering together, so the letters of these words are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Attending church with us is something nobody has actually mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congregation' rearranges ATTEND US into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never put into words has been left unspoken.

clue.text: Assert struggle looks hard

indicators.note: letters that struggle wrestle themselves into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone asserts themselves and battles on, glaring fiercely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggle' rearranges ASSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze fixedly and intently at someone is to look hard at them.

clue.text: Rent owing to regiment

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run on into regiment is a coincidence, not a hidden word
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army regiment

explanation.surface: Money owed in rent payable to a military regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment, but it is the past tense of rend, to rip.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the past form of rend, meaning ripped apart.

clue.text: An obvious choice of shoe material

definitions.meaning: the glossy varnished leather used for smart shoes

explanation.surface: An evident preference in the leather used for shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means plainly evident, and is also short for the shiny lacquered leather of dress shoes.

clue.text: Missiles always coldly deployed

parts.note: projectiles that, being made of packed frozen flakes, can only ever be thrown cold, as in a winter fight

explanation.surface: Weapons are always used in a calculating, unfeeling way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coldly' suggests ruthlessness, but the missiles are literally cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Packed frozen balls are thrown as missiles in winter play, and are cold by nature.

clue.text: Punishment for the mother country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A penalty to be inflicted on behalf of the motherland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother country' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal condemnation to hell is the ultimate punishment.

clue.text: A Dutch uncle's wife may be off-putting

parts.note: an uncle's wife is your aunt

explanation.surface: The wife of a stern, lecturing relative may discourage visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Dutch uncle' is an idiom for someone who lectures sternly; here the phrase breaks into D plus the uncle's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage or intimidate someone is to put them off.

clue.text: Small oval container?

parts.note: the oval thing contained is a breakfast item, and this is the little holder it sits in at the table

explanation.surface: A modest egg-shaped box of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oval' seems to describe the container's shape, but it describes what goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The small breakfast-table holder is made to contain a boiled oval shell.

clue.text: A former or practising priest

parts.note: past means former, as in a past president

explanation.surface: A clergyman who may be retired or still serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister in charge of a congregation is a working clergyman.

clue.text: Night predator taking two birds

parts.note: the first bird is a large raptor
the second bird is a nocturnal hunter

explanation.surface: A nocturnal hunter catches a pair of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This huge Eurasian owl hunts after dark and preys on mammals and birds.

clue.text: Sister sat back in a state of equilibrium

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits within the shortened sister
back says the word sat is written in reverse order

explanation.surface: A nun sat back, entirely calm and balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word sat around, and 'in' sets that inside the short form of sister; the definition is the clue's last words.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a condition of balance where nothing changes.

clue.text: So this crew is reliable as recording artists?

definitions.meaning: So ... Crew were a London garage music collective, so this word completes their name

explanation.surface: A dependable band of people, as the recording industry would describe them.
explanation.walkthrough: So Solid Crew were a British garage group with hit records around 2001; 'as recording artists' tells you the crew is that band.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm and dependable can be relied on.

clue.text: Old china animal, a thing farmers make

parts.note: a cat is an animal
farmers make hay while the sun shines

explanation.surface: An antique porcelain animal, plus something a farmer produces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like porcelain, but it is the country, here given its old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the medieval European name for the land of China.

clue.text: The beggar will fix it, working in tin

parts.note: to mend is to fix

indicators.note: working in says the second word is set to work inside the first, splitting it

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A tramp offers to repair something by labouring in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working in' sets tin's synonym to work inside the word it, splitting it around the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant lives by asking for alms, as a beggar does.

clue.text: A bit of jewellery could be commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial on TV

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery might be advertised on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial' looks like an adjective but is the noun for an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A small threaded ball is strung on necklaces and bracelets.

clue.text: At college, positive identification of tumour

parts.note: POLY is short for polytechnic, a type of British college

explanation.surface: Doctors at a college confirm the identity of a growth.
explanation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a British higher-education college, abbreviated POLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small growth projecting from a mucous membrane, a kind of tumour.

clue.text: Probably first legal document will get approval

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word probably

parts.note: a lease is a legal document granting tenancy

explanation.surface: A lawyer's first document will probably be approved.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to win someone's satisfaction or favour.

clue.text: Dance over by six

definitions.meaning: in cricket an over is six deliveries, so one delivery is an over divided by six

explanation.surface: A dance overrun by six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, each called a ball; 'by' means divided by.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a formal dance and also a single cricket delivery, one sixth of an over.

clue.text: Bandits seizing ship and heading south

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

explanation.surface: Outlaws take a vessel and sail it south.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigands are robbers who live outside the law, as bandits do.

clue.text: Does he read badly? Stick at it!

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Encouraging a poor reader to persevere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges HE READ.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or hold fast to something is to stick to it.

clue.text: Breaks through, achieving backstreet clean-up

indicators.note: in a down clue up says these pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a backstreet is a street, abbreviated ST
pure means clean

explanation.surface: Bursting out while tidying a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ST PURE backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that erupts bursts out through the ground's surface.

clue.text: American prosecutor gets firm — it's necessary to catch robber

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US
CO is short for company, a firm
the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A US lawyer gets the company to catch a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: A dacoit is a member of an armed gang of robbers in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacoit is an Indian bandit who robs in a gang.

clue.text: Steps first taken in Paris to produce food containers

parts.note: a can is a tin for food
a second tin for food

explanation.surface: Early steps in the French capital lead to tinned food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' is the definition: the high-kicking dance began in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking dance that originated in Parisian dance halls.

clue.text: The girl's an ass!

explanation.surface: Calling a girl a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name and also the word for a female donkey.

clue.text: Washes thoroughly in prison and in court

parts.note: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison, often just called Scrubs
a defendant who is up is before the court

explanation.surface: Someone cleans up thoroughly while in jail and at trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a well-known London prison; being 'up' before a judge means on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wash their hands and arms thoroughly before operating.

clue.text: Look noble

explanation.surface: A distinguished aristocratic appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to gaze searchingly and also a lord of the realm.

clue.text: Point to a number that are tidy

parts.note: NE is northeast, a compass point
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Pointing to several things that are neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point, NE.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to put in order, a verb meaning tidy.

clue.text: Some sign at sunset of annoying insects

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Swarms of irritating bugs appear at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of SIGN AT SUNSET.
explanation.definitionFit: These small biting flies swarm and irritate people.

clue.text: Needing attention and insisting on it

definitions.meaning: requiring a lot of effort or care

explanation.surface: Someone who wants attention and won't stop asking for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxing child needs much care, and a person who requires something firmly is insisting.
